paper.instructions:
(i) This Question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
(ii) Question paper is divided into FIVE Sections – Section A, B, C, D and E.
(iii) In Section A – Question Number 1 to 18 are Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) and Question Number 19 & 20 are Assertion-Reason based questions of 1 mark each.
(iv) In Section B – Question Number 21 to 25 are Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions, carrying 2 marks each.
(v) In Section C – Question Number 26 to 31 are Short Answer (SA) type questions, carrying 3 marks each.
(vi) In Section D – Question Number 32 to 35 are Long Answer (LA) type questions, carrying 5 marks each.
(vii) In Section E – Question Number 36 to 38 are case study based questions, carrying 4 marks each.
(viii) There is no overall choice. However, an internal choice has been provided in few questions in all the Sections except Section – A.
(ix) Use of calculator is NOT allowed.

questions.stem:
Check whether function $f(x)$ defined as
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{|x-3|}{2(x-3)}, & x < 3 \\ \dfrac{x-6}{6}, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$$
is continuous at $x = 3$ or not?
questions.solution:
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{-(x-3)}{2(x-3)}, & x < 3 \\ \dfrac{x-6}{6}, & x \ge 3 \end{cases} \Rightarrow f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{-1}{2}, & x < 3 \\ \dfrac{x-6}{6}, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$$
$f(3) = \frac{-1}{2}$
LHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} \frac{-1}{2} = \frac{-1}{2}$ (1)
RHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} \frac{x-6}{6} = \frac{-1}{2}$ (½)
LHL = RHL = $f(3)$, hence the function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 3$. (½)
questions.or_solution:
Differentiating both sides w.r.to $x$, we get $\sqrt{3}\left(2x + 2y\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = 4\left(x\frac{dy}{dx} + y\right)$ (1)
$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2y - \sqrt{3}x}{\sqrt{3}y - 2x}$ (½)
$\Rightarrow \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_{\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{3}$ (½)

questions.stem: A room freshner bottle in the shape of an inverted cone sprays the perfume at regular intervals such that volume of the perfume in the bottle decreases at the steady rate of $1\ \mathrm{mm^{3}/min}$. Find the rate at which level of perfume is dropping at an instant when level of perfume in the bottle is $10\ \mathrm{mm}$, if the semi-vertical angle of conical bottle is $\frac{\pi}{6}$.
questions.solution:
Let v, r, h, respectively, be the volume, radius and the height of perfume at any time t.
$\frac{dv}{dt} = -1\ \mathrm{mm^{3}/min}$
$\frac{r}{h} = \tan\frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow r = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$ (½)
$v = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h = \frac{1}{3}\pi\frac{h^{3}}{3}$ (½)
$\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{9}3h^{2}\frac{dh}{dt}$ (½)
$\Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{3}{\pi h^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \left(\frac{dh}{dt}\right)_{h=10} = -\frac{3}{100\pi}$ (½)
The level of perfume is dropping at the rate of $\frac{3}{100\pi}\ \mathrm{mm/min}$

questions.stem: Find the vector of magnitude 14 in the direction of $\overrightarrow{QP}$, where P and Q are the points $(1, 3, 2)$ and $(-1, 0, 8)$ respectively.
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{QP} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 6\hat{k}$ (½)
$|\overrightarrow{QP}| = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = 7$ (½)
The unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{QP} = \frac{\overrightarrow{QP}}{|\overrightarrow{QP}|} = \frac{2}{7}\hat{i} + \frac{3}{7}\hat{j} - \frac{6}{7}\hat{k}$
The required vector $= 14\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{QP}}{|\overrightarrow{QP}|}\right) = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}$ (1)

questions.stem: Vectors $\vec{a} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{k}$ represent the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram. Find the vectors representing its diagonals and hence find their lengths.
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = 4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$, $\vec{a} - \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$
The vector representing one of its diagonals is $4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ or $-(4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ (½)
The vector representing the other diagonal is $2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$ or $-(2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})$ (½)
The lengths of the two diagonals are $\sqrt{16 + 4 + 16} = 6$ and $\sqrt{4 + 4} = 2\sqrt{2}$ (1)

questions.or_solution:
Put $x^{2} = t$ to get $\frac{x^{2}}{(x^{2}+9)(x^{2}+16)} = \frac{t}{(t+9)(t+16)} = \frac{A}{t+9} + \frac{B}{t+16}$ (½)
Getting $A = \frac{-9}{7}$, $B = \frac{16}{7}$ (1)
Given integral $= \frac{-9}{7}\int\frac{1}{x^{2}+9}\,dx + \frac{16}{7}\int\frac{1}{x^{2}+16}\,dx$ (½)
$= \frac{-3}{7}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) + \frac{4}{7}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + C$ (1)

questions.solution:
$I_1 = 2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\frac{dx}{1 + \cos 2x}$, $\quad\left(\frac{1}{1 + \cos 2x}\text{ is an even function}\right)$
$= 2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\frac{dx}{2\cos^{2}x} = \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sec^{2}x\,dx$
$= [\tan x]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} = 1$ (1½)
Note: Students attempting $I_1$ without the application of any property should be marked proportionately.
$I_2 = 2\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}|x|\,dx$, $\quad(|x|\text{ is an even function})$ (½)

$= [x^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{4}$ (½)
$I_1 - 4I_2 = 0$ (½)

questions.stem:
Find the general solution of the following differential equation:
$x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx} = x^{2} + xy + y^{2}$
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is $\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \frac{y}{x} + \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{2}$ (½)
Put $y = vx \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}$ (½)
The given differential equation becomes $x\frac{dv}{dx} = 1 + v^{2}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{1 + v^{2}} = \frac{dx}{x}$ (½)
$\Rightarrow \int\frac{dv}{1 + v^{2}} = \int\frac{dx}{x}$
$\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}v = \log|x| + C$ (1)
$\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = \log|x| + C$ (½)
questions.or_stem:
Find the particular solution of the differential equation
$xy\frac{dy}{dx} = (x + 2)(y + 2)$, given that $y(1) = -1$.
questions.or_solution:
Given differential equation is $\frac{y}{y+2}\,dy = \frac{(x+2)}{x}\,dx$ (1)
$\Rightarrow \int\left(1 - \frac{2}{y+2}\right)dy = \int\left(1 + \frac{2}{x}\right)dx$
$\Rightarrow y - 2\log|y+2| = x + 2\log|x| + C$ or $y = x + 2\log|x(y+2)| + C$. (1½)
When $x = 1, y = -1 \Rightarrow C = -2$
The required particular solution is
$y - 2\log|y+2| = x + 2\log|x| - 2$ or $y = x + 2\log|x(y+2)| - 2$ (½)

questions.stem:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically:
Minimize $\quad Z = 13x - 15y$
Subject to constraints
$x + y \le 7,$
$2x - 3y + 6 \ge 0,$
$x \ge 0, y \ge 0$
questions.solution:
Graph of the constraints with the feasible region shaded (see figure): corner points $(0, 0)$, $(7, 0)$, $(3, 4)$, $(0, 2)$. (1½, correct graph and shading)
Corner point | Value of $Z = 13x - 15y$
$(0, 0)$ | $0$
$(7, 0)$ | $91$
$(3, 4)$ | $-21$
$(0, 2)$ | $-30$ (1)
The minimum value of Z is $-30$ at $x = 0, y = 2$ (½)

questions.stem: Out of two bags, bag I contains 3 red and 4 white balls and bag II contains 8 red and 6 white balls. A die is thrown. If it shows a number less than 3 then a ball is drawn at random from bag I, otherwise a ball is drawn at random from bag II. Find the probability that the ball drawn from one of the bags is a red ball.
questions.solution:
Let $E_1$: The number appearing on the die $< 3$
$E_2$: The number appearing on the die $\ge 3$
A: Red ball is drawn (½)
$P(E_1) = \frac{2}{6}, P(A/E_1) = \frac{3}{7}, P(E_2) = \frac{4}{6}, P(A/E_2) = \frac{8}{14}$ (1)
The required probability $= P(A) = P(E_1)P(A/E_1) + P(E_2)P(A/E_2)$
$= \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{3}{7} + \frac{4}{6} \times \frac{8}{14}$ (1)
$= \frac{11}{21}$ (½)
questions.or_stem: The probability of simultaneous occurrence of atleast one of the two events X and Y is a. If the probability that exactly one of the events X, Y occurs is b, prove that $P(X') + P(Y') = 2 - 2a + b$.

questions.stem:
A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as
$$R = \{(x, y) : |x - y| \text{ is divisible by a prime number `p'},\ x, y \in Z\}$$
check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.
questions.solution:
Let $x \in Z$. Then $|x - x| = 0$, which is divisible by a prime number p.
Hence, $(x, x) \in R$. Thus, R is reflexive. (1½)
Let $x, y \in Z$ such that $(x, y) \in R$.
Then $|x - y|$ is divisible by the prime number p.
$\Rightarrow |y - x|$ is divisible by the prime number p as $|x - y| = |y - x|$
Hence, $(y, x) \in R$. Thus, R is symmetric. (1½)
Let $x, y, z \in Z$ such that $(x, y), (y, z) \in R$.
Then $|x - y|$ is divisible by the prime number p and $|y - z|$ is divisible by the prime number p.
$\Rightarrow x - y$ is divisible by the prime number p and $y - z$ is divisible by the prime number p.
$\Rightarrow x - y + y - z$ is divisible by the prime number p
$\Rightarrow x - z$ is divisible by the prime number p
$\Rightarrow |x - z|$ is divisible by the prime number p
Hence, $(x, z) \in R$. Thus, R is transitive. (1½)
Since, R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, therefore, R is an equivalence relation. (½)
questions.or_stem: A function $f : R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\} \longrightarrow R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\}$ is defined as $f(x) = \frac{3x + 2}{5x - 3}$. Show that f is one-one and onto.
questions.or_solution:
Let $x_1, x_2 \in R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\}$ such that $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{3x_1 + 2}{5x_1 - 3} = \frac{3x_2 + 2}{5x_2 - 3}$
$\Rightarrow 15x_1x_2 - 9x_1 + 10x_2 - 6 = 15x_1x_2 + 10x_1 - 9x_2 - 6$
$\Rightarrow x_1 = x_2$
Hence, f is one-one. (2½)
Let $y \in R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\}$ (Codomain).
Then $f(x) = y$
or, $\frac{3x + 2}{5x - 3} = y \Rightarrow x = \frac{3y + 2}{5y - 3} \in$ Domain.
Hence, for every $y \in R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\}$ (codomain),
there exists $x = \frac{3y + 2}{5y - 3} \in R - \left\{\frac{3}{5}\right\}$ (domain) such that $f\left(\frac{3y + 2}{5y - 3}\right) = y$
Thus, f is onto. (2½)

questions.stem:
If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{-1}$ and use it to solve the following system of equations :
$-2y + z = 7,\ 2x - y - z = 8,\ x - 2y = 10$
questions.solution:
$|A| = -2(2) + 1(3) = -1 \neq 0$ (1)
$\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -1 & -3 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ (1½)
$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -2 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$ (½)
Given system of equations is equivalent to $A^{T}X = B$, where $X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}, B = \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 8 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}$ (½)
$X = (A^{T})^{-1}B = (A^{-1})^{T}B$
$\Rightarrow \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 8 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}$ (1½)
$\therefore x = 0, y = -5, z = -3$
questions.or_stem: If $\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & \sin 3x \\ -7 & 4 & \cos 2x \\ -11 & 7 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is a singular matrix, then find all values of $x$ where $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$.
questions.or_solution:
Given matrix is singular, hence, its determinant = 0,
i.e., $\begin{vmatrix} 3 & -1 & \sin 3x \\ -7 & 4 & \cos 2x \\ -11 & 7 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$ (1)
$\Rightarrow 2\cos 2x + \sin 3x = 2$ (1)
$\Rightarrow 4\sin^{3}x + 4\sin^{2}x - 3\sin x = 0$ (1)
$\Rightarrow \sin x(4\sin^{2}x + 4\sin x - 3) = 0$
$\Rightarrow \sin x(2\sin x - 1)(2\sin x + 3) = 0$ (1)
Solving to get $x = 0, \frac{\pi}{6}$ (1)

questions.stem: If $x = \cos t$, $y = \cos mt$, prove that $(1 - x^{2})\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - x\frac{dy}{dx} + m^{2}y = 0$.
questions.solution:
$\frac{dx}{dt} = -\sin t, \frac{dy}{dt} = -m \times \sin(mt)$ (1)
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{m \times \sin(mt)}{\sin t}$ or $\sin t\frac{dy}{dx} = m \times \sin(mt)$ (1)
$\Rightarrow \sin t\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \frac{dy}{dx}\cos t \times \frac{dt}{dx} = m^{2}\cos(mt) \times \frac{dt}{dx}$ (2)
$\Rightarrow (1 - \cos^{2}t)\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - x\frac{dy}{dx} = -m^{2}\cos(mt)$
$\Rightarrow (1 - x^{2})\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - x\frac{dy}{dx} + m^{2}y = 0$ (1)

questions.stem: Check whether the lines given by $\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{z - 3}{4}$ and $\frac{x - 4}{5} = \frac{y - 1}{2} = z$ are parallel or not. If parallel, find the distance between them, otherwise find their point of intersection, if the lines are intersecting.
questions.solution:
Drs of first line are $\langle 2, 3, 4 \rangle$
Drs of second line are $\langle 5, 2, 1 \rangle$ (1)
Drs of the two lines are not proportional. Hence, the lines are not parallel. (1)
Any point on the first line is $(2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda + 2, 4\lambda + 3)$
Any point on the second line is $(5\mu + 4, 2\mu + 1, \mu)$ (1)
For the lines to intersect, we must have some $\lambda$ and $\mu$, for which these coordinates must coincide, i.e., we must have $2\lambda + 1 = 5\mu + 4,\ 3\lambda + 2 = 2\mu + 1,\ 4\lambda + 3 = \mu$, for some $\lambda$ and $\mu$
The first two equations, when solved, give us $\lambda = -1$ and $\mu = -1$. These values satisfy the third equation. Hence, the lines intersect. (1)
The point of intersection is $(-1, -1, -1)$ (1)

questions.stem:
An online delivery company in a city has 5000 subscribers and collects annual subscription fees of ₹ 300 per subscriber for unlimited free deliveries.

The company wishes to increase the annual subscription fee. It is predicted that, for every increase of ₹ 1, ten subscribers will discontinue. Assume that the company increased the annual fee by ₹ $x$.

Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
(i) How many subscribers will discontinue after an increase of ₹ $x$ in annual fee ? (1)
(ii) If $R(x)$ denotes the total revenue collected after the increase of ₹ $x$ in subscription fee, express $R(x)$ as a function of $x$. (1)
(iii) (a) Find the value of $x$ for which $R(x)$ is maximum. (2)
OR
(iii) (b) Find the sub-intervals of $(0, 5000)$ in which $R(x)$ is increasing and decreasing. (2)

In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹ 3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹ 2,00,000 each and three third prizes of ₹ 50,000 each.

A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets each costing ₹ 100 were sold there by raising a fund of ₹ 1,00,00,000.

Rohan bought one ticket.

Based on given information, answer the following questions :
(i) What are the possible amounts, the person can win ? (1)
(ii) (a) What is the probability that the person wins atleast ₹ 2,00,000 ? (2)
OR
(ii) (b) What is the probability that the person does not win any amount ? (2)
(iii) In another jackpot, Rohan also bought a ticket having a prize money of ₹ 5,00,000. The chances of winning the jackpot are 1 in 1,00,000. Find the probability that on exactly one of tickets he wins the jackpot. (1)
questions.solution:
(i) ₹ 300000, ₹ 200000, ₹ 50000 (1)
(ii) (a) Required probability $= \frac{3}{100000}$ (2)
OR
(ii) (b) Required probability $= 1 - \frac{6}{100000} = \frac{99994}{100000}$ or $\frac{49997}{50000}$ (2)
(iii) P (Exactly on one of the tickets Rohan wins the jackpot) = P [(He wins first and he loses second) or (He loses first and wins second)]
$= \frac{6}{100000} \times \frac{99999}{100000} + \frac{99994}{100000} \times \frac{1}{100000} = \frac{699988}{10^{10}}$ or $\frac{174997}{2500000000}$ (1)

questions.stem:
Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights.

One such round-about is made such that equation representing its boundary is given by $C_1 ;\ x^{2} + y^{2} = 64$.

There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is given by $C_2 : x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$.

Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
(i) Represent the given equations $C_1$ and $C_2$ with the help of a diagram. (1)
(ii) Express y as a function of $x$, $(y = f(x))$, for both $C_1$ an $C_2$. (1)
(iii) (a) Using integration find the area of region covered by the roundabout. (2)
OR
(iii) (b) Using integration, find the area of region covered by circular pond. (2)
questions.solution:
(i) Diagram of $C_1$ and $C_2$ (see figure). (1)
(ii) Circle $C_1$: $y = \sqrt{64 - x^{2}}$ or $y = -\sqrt{64 - x^{2}}$ (½)
Circle $C_2$: $y = \sqrt{4 - x^{2}}$ or $y = -\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}$ (½)
(iii) (a) Required area $= 4 \times \int_{0}^{8} \sqrt{64 - x^{2}}\,dx$ (1)
$= 2\left[x\sqrt{64 - x^{2}} + 64\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{8}\right]_{0}^{8} = 64\pi$ (1)
OR
(iii) (b) Required area $= 4 \times \int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^{2}}\,dx$ (1)
$= 2\left[x\sqrt{4 - x^{2}} + 4\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{2}\right]_{0}^{2} = 4\pi$ (1)
